title: The road to Paranal
caption: The landscape around the Very Large Telescope, Cerro Paranal
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Small silver shapes sit on a distant mountaintop, far across a bare landscape that looks almost like an alien world. They are the telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) on Cerro Paranal in Chile. ESO gave the photograph the title "The road to Paranal".

The shapes belong to two kinds of instrument. The larger ones are the VLT's Unit Telescopes, and the smaller ones are its Auxiliary Telescopes. From this distance they shrink to specks, which gives a feel for how much empty ground surrounds the observatory.

The photographer, Y. Beletsky, took the picture from a neighbouring peak. That mountain is an observing site in its own right, home to another ESO facility, the Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy, known as VISTA. The two summits are close enough that one observatory can be photographed from the other.
